question: May a top-level `userTokenReadOnly: false` begin enabling writes for existing child Slack accounts that omitted the setting, or must writable user identity remain an explicit per-account opt-in?
rationale: The PR intentionally changes a credential-write boundary for stored multi-account configurations; tests can prove behavior, but only maintainers can approve whether that upgrade semantic is acceptable.

options.title: Require per-account opt-in
options.body: Keep omitted child accounts read-only and require `userTokenReadOnly: false` on each account that may post as a Slack user.

options.title: Adopt inherited writes
options.body: Allow root `false` to inherit into child accounts, but explicitly approve the security change and add upgrade documentation and regression proof for existing configs.

recommendation.title: Require per-account opt-in
recommendation.body: Keep omitted child accounts read-only and require `userTokenReadOnly: false` on each account that may post as a Slack user.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history in the Slack monitor and configuration paths and are best positioned to decide this credential boundary.
